claims: C1 the assistant must adhere to the Model Spec above all else
C2 default instructions in the Model Spec sit at the user or guideline authority level
C3 users or developers may override default instructions

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; model and assistant are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: default_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is a default instruction in the Model Spec that sits at the user or guideline authority level and may be overridden

concepts.name: user_or_developer
concepts.gloss: Actor is a user or developer who interacts with the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause says defaults can be overridden by users or developers; a class is needed to identify which actors qualify

concepts.name: instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction appearing in the Model Spec
concepts.inference: the clause classifies instructions in the Model Spec as default, so there must be a predicate picking out the instructions being classified

concepts.name: instruction_authority_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I sits at authority level L in the hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause sorts default instructions by authority level, so instructions must carry a level

ontology.gloss: Actor counts as a user or developer because Actor is a user
ontology.inference: users are one of the two actor kinds the clause names as able to override defaults

ontology.gloss: Actor counts as a user or developer because Actor is a developer
ontology.inference: developers are one of the two actor kinds the clause names as able to override defaults

ontology.gloss: I is a user-level instruction in the Model Spec, hence a default instruction
I is a guideline-level instruction in the Model Spec, hence a default instruction

asserts.read_back: % must adhere to the Model Spec above all else

closure.reason: the clause obliges the assistant to adhere to the Model Spec but does not directly prohibit any other act, so silence leaves other acts permitted
the clause explicitly permits users and developers to override default instructions but does not address other actors, so silence is unsettled for them
